extracted.intended_audience: programmers and users writing MetaPost code and macros (MetaPost graphics/TeX integrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and language rules for defining and using MetaPost macros, loops, file I/O, output settings, previewing PostScript, and debugging in MetaPost programs. Targets producing correct, portable, and well-formed MetaPost graphics and scripts for TeX integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro call parameter separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameters in a macro call can be separated by commas or by ")(" pairs. The only restriction is that a text parameter must be followed by a right parenthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: foo(a,b)(c) sets the text parameter to “a,b” and the expr parameter to c; while foo(a,b,c) sets the text parameter to “a,b,c” and leaves the interpreter still looking for an expr parameter. Be careful: if a macro expects a text parameter followed by an expr parameter, using comma-separated parameters may change which tokens go into the text parameter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vardef for function-like macros
rubrics_metrics.description: A macro definition can begin with vardef instead of def. Vardef macros are particularly well-suited to applications where macros are being used like functions or subroutines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vardef behaves like a variable of type 'macro'; begingroup and endgroup are automatically inserted at beginning and end of replacement text so the macro acts like a subroutine. General rule: use vardef if you intend the macro to be used like a function or subroutine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vardef supports multi-token names and generic subscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a vardef macro can be more than one token long and it can contain subscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a vardef macro has generic subscripts, numeric values must be given when the macro is called. Implicit suffix parameters #@ and @ are provided to distinguish calls (e.g., #@ is everything before last token, @ is last token). Example: vardef a[]b(expr p) = ... enddef; then a2b((1,2)) and a3b((1,2)..(3,4)) are valid calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suffix parameters (#@ and @) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Every vardef macro has suffix parameters #@ and @, where @ is the last token in the name from the macro call and #@ is everything preceding the last token.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use #@ and @ to make replacement text sensitive to the macro name used (e.g., p shifted (#@,b)). Note: @ is a suffix parameter, not an expr parameter — expressions like @+1 are illegal. To access numeric values in @, extract them with str (see caution below).

rubrics_metrics.name: str operator for suffix inspection (emergency use)
rubrics_metrics.description: The str operator takes a suffix and returns a string representation of a suffix (e.g., str @ would be "3" in a.b3 and "3.14" in a.b3.14 or a.b[3.14]; negative subscripts return '[-3]').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The str operator is generally for emergency use only. Prefer to use suffix parameters as variable names or suffixes rather than parsing them as strings.

rubrics_metrics.name: vardef @# suffix form
rubrics_metrics.description: vardef ⟨generic variable⟩@# is an alternative that makes the interpreter look for a suffix following the name given in the macro call and makes this available as the @# suffix parameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables macros that act on following suffixes (example: vardef z@#=(x@#,y@#) enddef; so z.a1 refers to x.a1 and y.a1). Use when you want the macro to capture a following suffix token.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to prefer def vs vardef (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison points: vardef macros are auto-grouped with begingroup/endgroup; names may be multi-token and contain subscripts; vardef macros can access suffix following macro name; symbolic tokens in vardef names remain tags and can be used in other variable names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need grouping behavior, multi-token names/subscripts, or suffix access, prefer vardef. Otherwise def is usually sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining unary/primary/secondary/tertiary operator-like macros
rubrics_metrics.description: Macros can be defined to behave like unary operators (primary/secondary/tertiary) or binary operators using definitions like 'vardef round primary u = ...', 'def fill expr c = ...', 'vardef direction expr t of p = ...', 'primarydef w dotprod z = ...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate def form (vardef, def, primarydef, secondarydef, tertiarydef) to match the argument syntax you want. Note: primarydef/secondarydef/tertiarydef define ordinary macros, not vardef macros; there is no 'primaryvardef'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro parameter grammar and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Macro parameters can have a delimited part and an undelimited part; parameter types are expr, suffix, or text; undelimited parts may be empty or specify precedence (primary/secondary/tertiary) or expr of parameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: def foo(text a) expr b = ... enddef defines a text parameter in parentheses followed by an expression. The formal grammar (Figure 51) should be consulted when writing complex macro headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undelimited suffix parameter behavior (incr/decr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Undelimited suffix parameters (e.g., vardef incr suffix $ = $:=$+1; $ enddef;) make macros that take a variable as a suffix; undelimited suffix parameters may be parenthesized so both incr a and incr(a) are legal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use undelimited suffix parameters when you want to treat the argument as a variable name/suffix. Be careful with parentheses and variable types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undelimited text parameter runs to statement end
rubrics_metrics.description: An undelimited text parameter is the list of tokens following the macro call up to the first ';' or 'endgroup' or 'end', except that an argument containing 'begingroup' will include the matching 'endgroup'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: def cutdraw text t = begingroup interim linecap:=butt; draw t; endgroup enddef; — cutdraw is like draw but changes linecap. Remember undelimited text parameters absorb everything until statement terminators.

rubrics_metrics.name: For loops: progression and step semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: for i=a step b until c scans i values a, a+b, a+2b, ... stopping before i passes c (i ≤ c if b>0, i ≥ c if b<0). For b=0 the loop never terminates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid non-integer step sizes because fixed-point arithmetic error can accumulate (example: for i=0 step .1 until 1 yields last value 0.90005). Standard workaround: iterate over integer values and multiply by a scale factor, or give explicit sequence expressions separated by commas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loop body flexiblity and loop-index immutability
rubrics_metrics.description: A loop body can be virtually any sequence of tokens as long as they make sense together; a loop is like a macro definition followed by calls to the macro. The loop index behaves like an expr parameter: it can represent any value but is not a variable and cannot be changed by assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to modify the loop index inside the loop, use a forsuffixes loop (loop index behaves like a suffix parameter) or other constructs. Be careful when using loop body directly in drawing statements (draw for p=...: p-- endfor cycle equivalent to draw (list)--cycle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forsuffixes loops for suffix-style indices
rubrics_metrics.description: forsuffixes ⟨symbolic token⟩ = ⟨suffix list⟩ : ⟨loop text⟩ endfor makes the loop index behave like a suffix parameter; the suffix list is a comma-separated list of suffixes and empty suffixes are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common use: handling variable-length comma-separated lists passed to macros (e.g., vardef dotlabels@#(text t) = forsuffixes $=t: dotlabel@#(str$,z$); endfor enddef;). Ensure the parameter is a comma-separated list of suffixes when using forsuffixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loop exit constructs (exitif and exitunless)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any for, forever, or forsuffixes loop can contain exit clauses. Use 'exitif ⟨boolean expression⟩;' to exit when expression becomes true; 'exitunless' exits when expression becomes false. MetaPost's while-loop equivalent: forever: exitunless ⟨boolean expression⟩; ⟨loop text⟩ endfor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place exit clauses anywhere in the loop text; they cause evaluation of the boolean expression and exit the current loop if condition is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: readfrom returns next line or EOF string
rubrics_metrics.description: readfrom ⟨file name⟩ returns a string giving the next line of input from the named file. If the file has ended or cannot be read, the result is a string consisting of a single null character; the preloaded plain macro package introduces the name EOF for this string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After readfrom returns EOF, additional reads from the same file cause the file to be reread from the start. All files opened by readfrom that have not been completely read are closed automatically at program termination, but you should manually close files you don't need to read completely to avoid resource/capacity errors (use closefrom ⟨file name⟩).

rubrics_metrics.name: write to file and EOF semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: write ⟨string expression⟩ to ⟨file name⟩ writes a line of text to the specified output file, opening the file first if necessary. All such files are closed automatically when the program terminates. EOF as the ⟨string expression⟩ explicitly closes the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only way to tell if a write command has succeeded is to close the file and use readfrom to look at it. Use EOF to close files when done to ensure writes are flushed.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEX.mp for typesetting MetaPost strings
rubrics_metrics.description: TEX.mp provides a way to typeset the text of a MetaPost string expression. TEXPRE and TEXPOST values are included before and after each call to TEX; otherwise each TEX call is effectively typeset independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: TEXPRE("%&latex" & char(10) & "\documentclass{article}\begin{document}"); TEXPOST("\end{document}"); label(TEX("\( n_{" & decimal(i) & "}\)"), (5mm*i,0)); Use %&magic to invoke different TeX processors. Note: TEX \special instructions vanish and packages like xcolor and hyperref cannot be used via this route.

rubrics_metrics.name: outputtemplate for flexible output filenames
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigning a string with printf-style escape sequences to outputtemplate configures output filenames; default is %j.%c. Escape sequences include %j, %c, %y, %m, %d, %H, %M and %{⟨internal variable⟩}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-letter numeric escapes are rounded and can include a minimum digit width like %2m. For backwards compatibility %c evaluates to 'ps' if rounded charcode is negative; use %{charcode} to bypass special-case handling. Use outputtemplate to make file names meaningful (e.g., outputtemplate := "%j-%c.mps"). Assigning an empty string reverts to default.

rubrics_metrics.name: outputformat and outputformatoptions for format control
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost can generate EPSF, SVG (v1.1), or PNG. The internal string variable outputformat controls the format ('svg' or 'png' enable those outputs; other values fall back to PostScript). Variable outputformatoptions is a string of key=value pairs that control bitmap conversion (e.g., format and antialias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default outputformat is 'eps'. outputformat is case-sensitive (e.g., 'SVG' falls back to PostScript). Example: outputformatoptions := "format=rgba antialias=fast". Keys not given are reset to default. By default outputformatoptions is empty.

rubrics_metrics.name: PNG conversion color handling and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: For PNG output, MetaPost converts all colors found in a picture to RGB, then possibly to gray if requested; CMYK→RGB conversion uses r=1−k−c, g=1−k−m, b=1−k−y (clipped to [0,1]). Gray intensity j = 0.2126·r + 0.7152·g + 0.0722·b. PNG backgrounds are transparent if format supports alpha.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colors are exact in PNG output only if input and output color spaces are compatible. Users who care about color conversion should apply transformations explicitly inside an extra_endfig loop. MetaPost has no built-in color management; built-in conversions are a convenience only.

rubrics_metrics.name: hppp and vppp meaning in PNG backend
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables hppp and vppp are used by the PNG backend to decide the scale of the generated bitmap. In MetaPost they refer to points per pixel (not pixels per point as in METAFONT); values larger than 1 yield smaller dimensions. Default is 1.0 (one MetaPost point per pixel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the reversed meaning compared to METAFONT when setting these variables to control bitmap resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: mpprocset PostScript dictionary option
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting the internal variable mpprocset to 1 makes MetaPost create an extended PostScript preamble that defines a dictionary of abbreviations of PostScript commands (e.g., l for lineto) to reduce output file size. Default is 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mpprocset is relevant only for PostScript output (not SVG/PNG). Set to 1 to reduce file size at the cost of a more complex preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: prologues setting for bounding box and fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: prologues := 2 causes MetaPost to write PostScript that correctly identifies as Encapsulated PostScript so viewers obey bounding box; prologues := 3 embeds used PostScript fonts into the output file so labels render correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: put prologues := 2 before first beginfig to avoid viewer clipping; if glyphs are missing or wrong, use prologues := 3 (but embedding increases file size and may duplicate fonts across multiple graphics). Reset prologues to 0 before final inclusion of MetaPost graphics into external documents to avoid embedded fonts redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manual shifting workaround for bounding box
rubrics_metrics.description: A workaround to avoid clipping is currentpicture := currentpicture shifted -llcorner currentpicture; to move the lower-left corner to the origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This workaround is not recommended: it must be applied to all figures, clutters source code, alters coordinates in PostScript output (complicates debugging). Prefer setting prologues properly and configuring the PostScript viewer (e.g., GSview: Options → EPS Clip and Show Bounding Box).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof sheet tools for previewing multiple figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use provided plain TeX scripts mproof.tex and mpsproof.tex to collect many MetaPost output files into a proof sheet (multi-page document) for previewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mproof: tex mproof ⟨MetaPost output files⟩ creates a DVI proof sheet; mpsproof supports pdfTeX, has options like \noheaders and \bbox (bbox produces page sized to a figure's bounding box). Use shell globbing cautiously; consider setting outputtemplate to avoid matching source files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debugging: error message context and interactive responses
rubrics_metrics.description: When an error (e.g., undefined coordinate) occurs, the interpreter prints an '!' line with the error, context showing how much of each line has been read, and a '?' prompt. Context lines show descriptor and 'Text read so far' / 'Text yet to be read'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the '?' prompt possible responses include: x to terminate run and fix input; h to print help message; ⟨return⟩ to proceed best-effort. Use the context listing to locate the error (macro expansions, line numbers, etc.).
